title: [observability][recoverability] the transcript archive's failures are an alert: archive_failed fires once per occurrence ("... copies nothing: <reason>; unarchived since <time> UTC; at risk from Claude Code's cleanup"), stays one across a loop restart, and clears at the archive.resumed
prompt:
Spawn, objective 193 [observability][recoverability] (projects-47, 2026-11-15: the alert half of 179, split at the lead's word; the shape in sync/design-179-archive-failed.md b49db0c6; reviewers rev-e, then cc-astra): the transcript archive's failures are an alert. After [175, 179]: it reads 179's events, so it can be pushed only once the fleet has built 179.

Line: core line 6 [recoverability]; [observability].

Why. 175 fails closed: a pass that cannot have every credential value, or whose copy fails, copies nothing. Today the only signs are a loop log warning (said once per change of error) and the progress record's behind_ms, in a file under `<root>-progress`. 179 records each failure and its end as events; nothing raises an alert from them, so an archive can fall behind for days, until Claude Code's cleanup deletes the transcript it lacks.

What changes:
(1) crates/spawn-postgres/src/alerts.rs: ARCHIVES, `alert_archives(after)`: the archive events with id > after, in order, as JSON (event_id, name, agent_id, session_id, at_ms, native, reason). They are written on a change only, so the rows are few; the index on (event_name, recorded_at_ms) finds them.
(2) crates/spawn-cli/src/alerts.rs: `archive_failed`, subject the agent, key `archive_failed:<agent>:<native>:<the occurrence's first archive.failed>`.
  - The step reads the archive events when the log moved, after the last one it read. Its first read after a start begins at the first event, so a restarted loop rebuilds every occurrence before it applies a new one.
  - Per transcript, an occurrence runs from its first archive.failed after the last archive.resumed. A repeat (a restarted Bridge says it again) or a new reason changes only the reason; the occurrence keeps its first failure's id and time, and nothing more fires.
  - It fires once per occurrence, with evidence {agent_id, session_id, native, reason (scrubbed), since_ms, event_id} and the line "the transcript archive of <agent> (session <s>, native session <n>) copies nothing: <reason>; unarchived since <time> UTC; at risk from Claude Code's cleanup".
  - It clears at the transcript's next archive.resumed (the clear's event_id is after the fire's).
  - A session that ended while failing keeps it open: the line says the risk.
  - The module doc lists it.
Owner part: rsi/scenarios/193.sh (the contract). A tree without the alert (179 alone) fails it with 1 at (1): its missing alert is the failure, never setup.

Not in it (named next step): the "lost" state. When a transcript that ended unarchived is deleted by Claude Code's cleanup, the alert should say its bytes are lost, not still "failed". That needs the alert step to stat transcript paths on the host, a new reader with its own cost (the lead, 2026-11-14 00:0x). Also not in it: an alert from behind_ms itself (the progress files), and any change to what the archive copies.

Cost (polled read): one indexed read of the archive events after a cursor, per check where the log moved. Rows: the archive events written since the last check, on a change only (none in a healthy hour). For the lead's live timing: `explain (analyze, buffers) select count(*) from spawn_events e where e.event_name in ('archive.failed', 'archive.resumed') and e.id > (select max(id) - 10000 from spawn_events);`

Files: crates/spawn-postgres/src/alerts.rs, crates/spawn-cli/src/alerts.rs; rsi/scenarios/193.sh (owner).
Size (measured on the compiled branch against 179's tip, split at `mod tests`): code 180 (spawn-cli alerts.rs 159, spawn-postgres alerts.rs 21), tests 150; 193.sh 683 (owner; R2's (5)). The branch carries 179 R2's two commits cherry-picked (content-identical), so 193's diffs are taken from 179 R2's tip.

Acceptance: rsi/scenarios/193.sh, black box, on 175.sh's world.
(1) The credential rotated and its file unreadable, a BB:SAY turn: within 20 s `spawn alerts --once --json` holds one open archive_failed for the worker, its text naming the credential file's path and "at risk from Claude Code's cleanup"; no alert holds a form or a part of a value.
(2) A second turn, still unreadable: 8 s after it, still one archive_failed.
(3) The loop killed and started again by its runner, still unreadable, a third turn: 8 s after it, still one archive_failed for the worker, open, with the same key, whatever the restarted Bridge recorded again.
(4) The file readable again: within 20 s the alert is cleared.
(5) Unreadable again and a turn: a new archive_failed, open. The loop killed, the file made readable before its runner starts it again, and a turn: within 20 s both archive_failed are cleared (179 R2: the restarted Bridge ends the failure recorded before it).
On 179 alone and on main 6796e8c6, 193.sh exits 1 at (1). On 193 R1 (78cbf602, with 179 R1) it exits 1 at (5): the failure is never ended, so the alert stays open.

Tests (unit):
- alerts: a failure fires once and its resume clears it (repeat, new reason, new occurrence, another transcript); a restarted step rebuilds its occurrences from every event (resumed while down: cleared; still failing: no second alert); a transcript's new failure after its resume stays open; the reason is scrubbed in the line (a password in a URL is never in the text or the evidence).
No test is renamed or dropped.

R3 (cc-astra A79, A80, through the lead; A78 is 179 R3's, carried here):
- A79: the archive step reads its events in order; a resume clears each open archive_failed alert of its transcript that fired before it at once (open_archive_alerts), so a failure after it in the same read is a new occurrence and the clear stands.
- A80: the archive's events are read at the first check, even on a log that does not move (a restarted loop rebuilds every open occurrence), when the log moved, and again after a read that failed (archives_due).
Tests: alerts a_resume_then_a_failure_in_one_read_clears_the_old_alert_and_fires_the_new (unit: one read, and a restarted step); a_step_started_on_a_quiet_log_reads_the_archive_events_once (store: a failure recorded before the start fires at the first check; one recorded after a read that succeeded fires at the next). rev-g's n2: a read of the archive's events that failed is said and due again at the next check, set by the read's own answer (archives_read); test a_failed_archive_read_is_due_again_and_the_next_applies_its_events (unit). 179 R4's ARCHIVE_GONE failure fires archive_failed as any other. The A79 and A80 mutants (no in-order clear; not due at start; not due after a move; not due after a failed read) are killed by these tests only, because a live loop cannot reach the orders they depend on. The alert step runs in every pass where the log's watermark moved (crates/spawn-cli/src/commands/loops.rs:761, Schedule::runs: `mark != Some(watermark) || due <= now`). The Bridge whose appends move the watermark is in the same process and the same pass loop, so a resume and a later failure of one transcript are never in one read. A restarted loop's Bridge appends before the step's first check, so that first check never sees a quiet log. SPAWN_ALERT_CHECK_SECS only spaces the host readings, and no setting turns the step off. A scenario could only plant archive.* rows by SQL, a stub of the Bridge's record; the store test plants them against the real store.
